chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ishaq ibn al-Harith, from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Abdillah (AS) took out a small box, and from it he took out a piece of paper, and behold, it contained:

Glory be to the One, there is no god but He, the Eternal, the Originator without beginning, the Everlasting who does not tire, the Living who does not die, the Creator of what is seen and what is unseen, the Knower of all things without being taught, that is Allah who has no associate.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah mentioned in the creedal text from Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* highlights the transmission of a concise creedal formula (*mu'allaq*) attributed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS), serving as a foundational text for Shia theological affirmations of divine unity. It systematically negates anthropomorphism and partners by attributing attributes of perfection—such as being the Self-Sufficient Originator and All-Knowing without instruction—to Allah, while simultaneously affirming His transcendence over creation. This text underscores the Shia emphasis on *Tawhid* as both a metaphysical reality and a devotional practice preserved through reliable chains of transmission (*isnad*).

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 8. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn said on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of Ishaq ibn alHarith, on the authority of Abu Basir that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) took out a small box and took out from it a piece of paper, which had the following written on it:

Praise be to the One! There is no god but He. He is the Eternal, and the Originator without beginning. He is the Eternal, who does not tire. He is the Living, who does not die. He is the Creator of the seen and the unseen. He is the Knower of Everything without being taught. Such is Allah who has no associate.
